bundled.built_from: Taskwarrior 3.3.0 from https://github.com/GothenburgBitFactory/taskwarrior/releases/download/v3.3.0/task-3.3.0.tar.gz; compiled without source changes on Ubuntu 24.04 with GCC 13.3.0 and Rust 1.94.0 using cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build build && cmake --install build; strip --strip-unneeded bin/task. The archive contains the stripped task executable.

modifications: No upstream source changes. taskwarrior-tui is the upstream release binary; the Taskwarrior executable is locally built and stripped. Separate launchers apply Landlock restrictions.
configuration: Both applications use DATA_DIR as HOME. Taskwarrior creates its native .taskrc and .task data; taskwarrior-tui stores history below .local/share/taskwarrior-tui. The runtime supplies libfaketime 0.9.12 with a fixed wall clock and a running monotonic clock. Landlock permits only the two product programs and their loader to execute; writes are limited to private instance directories. Installed executables remain root-owned mode 0555. Before confinement the launcher creates mode-0111 executable copies under private TMPDIR; Landlock permits executing those copies and denies access to the installed implementation.

build.command: cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build build && cmake --install build; strip --strip-unneeded bin/task

libfaketime.build: The Dockerfile compiles the pinned release with make in src and installs it under /usr/local/lib/faketime.
